title: [YouPass Collect] - Living Alone Trends Across Age Groups in 1850-2000
prompt: The bar chart below shows the percentage of people living alone in 5 different age groups in the US from 1850 to 2000. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of Americans living alone across five age groups from 1850 to 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the percentages of people living alone in the three youngest age brackets remained relatively stable or declined slightly until 1950 before rising substantially by 2000, the two oldest age groups experienced more consistent growth throughout the latter half of the period. Additionally, the 55-64 age group recorded the most dramatic increase and the highest figure by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the younger demographics, in 1850, approximately 2.5% of individuals aged 17-26 and 27-36 lived alone, while the figure for the 37-46 bracket was slightly higher at 3%. By 1950, the first two groups had remained unchanged or decreased marginally to roughly 2.2% and 2.5% respectively, while the 37-46 age group dropped to around 2.8%. However, all three categories then surged significantly, reaching 5%, 8%, and 7% respectively in 2000.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the older age groups, those aged 47-54 started at 0% in 1850, increased to 3.5% by 1900, experienced a slight dip to around 3.2% in 1950, before rising dramatically to approximately 13% by 2000. An even more striking trend was observed in the 55-64 bracket, which remained at 0% until 1900, then jumped to nearly 10% in 1950, and ultimately surged to around 17% by the final year, becoming the highest proportion among all age groups.
